transcript:
Header:
Date: 2028-12-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lina Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Danny Ruíz (CTO - Orbitline), Maya Singh (SRE), Omar Khan (PM)
---
Auto-summary (auto): quick console walkthrough focused on per-route usage slices, cost breakdown, and pilot onboarding. Customer wants to validate per-route billing semantics and VPC/private data controls; concerned about SSO + SOC2 + KMS.
Topics: console usage lens, per-route dashboards, tag-based attribution, cost decomposition, trial dataset import, Dedicated vs Hosted routing, latency/cost tradeoffs.
Action items (captured): see metadata above.
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Lina Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining on a short notice, this is Lina from Redwood. we got Marcus on the call as well, our solutions engineer. how's that, uh, time for you all?
[00:12] Danny Ruíz: yeah looks good, thanks. morning for us here, afternoon for you. quick context - Orbitline's been piloting embedding routes and a few generation routes, and finance wants per-route chargeback.
[00:28] Marcus Patel: great, thanks Danny. real quick agenda, we'll show the Console usage lens, per-route dashboards, cost breakdowns, then walk through mapping your tags and a sample cost model. sound good?
[00:40] Maya Singh: yep that works. we're particularly interested in how the console attributes shared KV-cache and batching overhead to routes.
[00:51] Lina Chen: ok good, we'll call out batching policy assumptions. a heads-up transcription may show some product names weirdly, like K-V cash instead of KV cache, sorry in advance.
[01:05] Marcus Patel: opening the Console. so this is the usage homepage, token volume timeline across models and routes. if you look at the left nav, you can filter by route, model family, and time window.
[01:22] Marcus Patel: jumping to Route Summary. here's Orbitline's imaginary demo routes: search-embed, chat-assist, and render-summaries. each route has a per-token breakdown and a tokens-per-call distribution.
[01:35] Omar Khan: is that per-call median or p95?
[01:38] Marcus Patel: good call - the default view shows median and p90; you can toggle p50/p90/p99. the per-route cost estimate uses a cost model that includes: model price per token, inferred batching efficiency, and a KV-cache hit estimate. we try to be conservative on KV hits until you provide logs.
[01:55] Danny Ruíz: how do you attribute shared cache hits? e.g., if two routes hit the same prefix.
[02:02] Marcus Patel: currently we use a proportional attribution: if a prefix is shared we attribute cache savings proportional to the observed request volume that used that prefix. it's in the docs but we can run a separate attribution mode for you - the 'route-isolate' mode which charges cache at the originating route only.
[02:22] Maya Singh: that sounds important; our finance team will want the option for both. one more, encryption: do you support customer-managed keys?
[02:30] Lina Chen: yes, KMS/HSM integrations are available for Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys today; we can discuss bring-your-own-key options in Private mode.
[02:43] Omar Khan: what about audit logs and retention? we need 1 year of audit logs for some customers.
[02:48] Lina Chen: we offer extended retention as an add-on — configurable for up to 3 years. we also have SSO with SAML and RBAC roles.
[02:57] Marcus Patel: back to the UI, clicking into a route shows a timeline of requests, tokens, model variant, and importantly, a 'cost per call' waterfall. that waterfall breaks out model compute, batching discount (amortized), network egress, and storage/KV charges where applicable.
[03:15] Marcus Patel: note, the batching discount is an estimated effective delta relative to single-request cost; you can provide sample traffic and we'll calibrate the estimator.
[03:27] Danny Ruíz: can we export the per-route cost CSV? our internal chargeback system ingests CSVs.
[03:32] Marcus Patel: yes, export CSV and also an API endpoint to pull per-route slices daily.
[03:38] Maya Singh: show us a demo of a mis-attributed route, like when webhooks come from a third party and need re-routing.
[03:45] Marcus Patel: sure, i'll open the 'route explorer'. here's a route that had 20% external traffic; you can use the explorer to reclassify requests by header or tag and replay attribution. this is helpful when you have proxy headers that need mapping.
[04:02] Lina Chen: and on the cost side, the Console will surface the delta after reclassification so finance can see impact immediately.
[04:10] Omar Khan: nice. what about Dedicated? if we go dedicated, do we still get per-route insights?
[04:16] Marcus Patel: yes, Dedicated preserves the same telemetry and Console UX — the main differences are isolated GPU pools, reservation billing, and optional on-prem networking. the Console will show utilization and wasted capacity metrics too.
[04:29] Danny Ruíz: question on model fallback. if our primary model is down, how does Redwood route?
[04:34] Marcus Patel: we have smart routing policies — you can set failover to a compatible smaller model or to a cheaper region. the Console shows fallback logs and inferred quality delta if you want to run A/B or canary rollouts.
[04:49] Maya Singh: about quality, can we attach evals to specific prompt sets so we know a fallback is bad?
[04:54] Lina Chen: yes, Redwood Optimize allows tying quality monitors to prompt sets; you can alert on metric regressions and auto-fallback if thresholds cross.
[05:03] Marcus Patel: switching to Cost Breakdown view — at the top is 'cost by route', then 'cost by model', then 'unattributed system overhead'. system overhead includes batch scheduling, idle GPU time, and KV warmup. for pilots, we usually recommend adding a 10% amortized overhead line item until you have steady-state telemetry.
[05:25] Omar Khan: what's your unit price model? per-token only or per-req plus per-token?
[05:30] Lina Chen: Hosted is per-token with embedding units and generation tokens; Dedicated is reservation plus discounted per-token consumption for burst; Private is licensed. we'll send the SKU sheet.
[05:41] Danny Ruíz: do you support per-route budgets and alerts? we want to cap experimental routes.
[05:46] Marcus Patel: yes, route-level budgets and alerting via webhook or email; budgets can enforce soft or hard caps. hard cap returns a 429 or routes to a fallback.
[05:57] Maya Singh: is there an estimate of token-per-dollar for specific GPUs? we have a mix of A100 and H100 in our infra for other workloads.
[06:04] Marcus Patel: we provide model-level benchmarks and an effective token-per-dollar matrix for each hardware profile; for Hosted you'll see the unit economics in the Console. for Dedicated you pick GPU class in the reservation and we show throughput curves.
[06:20] Lina Chen: i'd like to show a short worked example — Marcus, can you load the demo dataset?
[06:26] Marcus Patel: loading sample traffic now. I'm going to filter to last 7 days. you'll see total spend $1,820, route 'render-summaries' is 42% of spend even though it's 28% of calls — because of longer context and lower cache hits.
[06:42] Omar Khan: that's the thing we suspected. can you show why the cache hit is low?
[06:46] Marcus Patel: sure — click into render-summaries -> 'cache diagnostics'. you'll see common prefixes and their hit rates; most are single-use prompts so cache doesn't help. suggestion: canonicalize prompts or move repeated prefixes to an embedding lookup route.
[07:03] Danny Ruíz: if we canonicalize, will the billing show reduced cost immediately?
[07:07] Marcus Patel: yes, the Console will simulate the projected delta given a hypothetical increase in KV hit rate — we have a slider to model 10/30/50% hits. you can then export the projection to CSV for finance.
[07:20] Maya Singh: potential compliance note: can the Console mask PII in logs for demo? we can't share real PII in trial org.
[07:27] Lina Chen: yes we have a redaction mode and pseudo-anonymization for demo installs; we'll enable it for your trial.
[07:35] Marcus Patel: also, for pilot onboarding we can pre-load synthetic traffic derived from your schema so you can see console metrics without exposing PII.
[07:44] Omar Khan: nice. what's the onboarding time for a pilot? two weeks?
[07:48] Lina Chen: typical pilot is 1-3 weeks: week one for trial provisioning and data import, week two run-day-to-day traffic, and an optional week three for a cost-quality review and SKUs discussion.
[08:00] Danny Ruíz: governance — can RBAC restrict who sees cost vs who sees traces?
[08:05] Marcus Patel: yes, role based access: billing viewers vs infra admins vs SRE can have different scopes.
[08:12] Maya Singh: about the per-route API export — can we integrate it into our Snowflake daily ingest?
[08:16] Marcus Patel: yep, the daily export is S3/CSV or push to your endpoint. we also have a partner connector for Snowflake via our ingestion lambda.
[08:26] Lina Chen: ok, quick pause — any blockers for a pilot?
[08:30] Omar Khan: procurement will need pricing and a sample COA. also legal will ask about data residency for EU customers.
[08:36] Lina Chen: we'll include EU region docs and data residency options in the security pack.
[08:42] Marcus Patel: showing the 'what-if' cost planner — you can input reserved capacity and see breakeven points. this is useful for deciding Dedicated vs Hosted.
[08:55] Danny Ruíz: what about sudden spikes? will autoscaling add crazy costs?
[09:00] Marcus Patel: autoscaling is constrained by policy; you can set burst caps and we support pre-warmed pools to limit cold spin costs. costs are still metered but can be amortized across reserved pools.
[09:12] Maya Singh: any caveats for on-prem Private installs? e.g., networking or latency to embeddings store?
[09:18] Lina Chen: Private you manage networking — we recommend colocating embeddings store or using a high-throughput link; Console still reports metrics but some agent instrumentation differs.
[09:28] Marcus Patel: switching to Demo -> Alerts page. here you can create a budget rule for 'render-summaries' route. set threshold 80% and action 'notify slack' + 'route-fallback to cheap-model'.
[09:44] Omar Khan: ok let's set that up in the trial.
[09:47] Marcus Patel: quick note on telemetry fidelity — we can ingest request-level logs but there's a cost to retention. default is aggregated slices; if you want request-level for a short window, we can enable it.
[10:00] Maya Singh: retention cost tradeoff noted.
[10:03] Danny Ruíz: curious about multi-tenant attribution if we share model capacity across products.
[10:09] Marcus Patel: Console supports tenant-aware routes; we do per-tenant and per-route slices and a combined view. for chargeback we recommend unique route naming and header-based tenant id.
[10:22] Lina Chen: ok wrapping up, we'll provision a trial org, enable redaction, load synthetic traffic, and share the security pack + pricing. Marcus will run a quick calibration of batching assumptions using their sample CSV.
[10:36] Omar Khan: question — is there a way to retro-fit insights from past logs? we have 30 days of logs in-house.
[10:42] Marcus Patel: yes, we can import historical logs and run attribution backfill; that takes 2-3 business days depending on volume.
[10:51] Maya Singh: perfect. last question: for billing exports, do we support hourly granularity?
[10:56] Marcus Patel: yes, hourly or daily granularity. hourly for high-fidelity chargeback.
[11:03] Danny Ruíz: ok thanks everyone, that was very helpful. we'll aim to share the sample traffic and confirm procurement dates by Friday.
[11:12] Lina Chen: great, thanks all. Marcus, anything to add?
[11:15] Marcus Patel: no, just that I'll follow up with the trial link and a short how-to doc for mapping headers to routes.
[11:22] Lina Chen: recap of next steps: send security pack (SOC2/KMS), provision trial org, customer to share traffic, schedule pilot kickoff. thanks all, bye.
[11:32] (call ends)
---
Notes on transcript quality: medium — occasional mis-attributions and auto-capitalization; product terms occasionally transcribed oddly (K-V cash, Optimise).
